messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] streaming p95/p99 breach detected for /v1/generate (model-serving). cluster=gpu-cluster-east p95=340ms p99=1.6s (SLO p99=400ms). severity=sev2. paging oncall. :bangbang:

leah: i'm oncall, acknowledging. starting triage. are we seeing error spike or just latency?

marco: from traces: token-gen stalls, many requests showing 'blocked waiting for kernel' on NVML calls. error rate low, but tail latency huge. KV cache RTTs spiked from 4ms -> 30ms for affected shards.

ops-bot: telemetry: node-g10 (gpu-cluster-east) reports GPU_THROTTLE=1, fan_rpm=0 (last seen 01:23 UTC), PCIe_link_down events x3 in 8m, NVML_recoveries=5.

tay: who owns node-g10? marco?

marco: ops team. i'm seeing kernel logs from node-g10 with repeated messages: 
```
[  +0.000123] NVRM: GPU 0000:65:00: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[  +0.001234] kernel: pcieport 0000:01:00.0: AER: Uncorrected (Non-Fatal) error: id=0000
[  +0.002345] nvme0n1: I/O 0x... error, dev nvme0n1, sector ...
```

leah: that looks like transient PCIe disconnects causing driver resets -> stalls. operations, can we evacuate pods from node-g10 and mark as quarantine?

ops-bot: initiating live-mitigation: cordon node-g10, start eviction. Note: many sessions are pinned (enterprise customers) -> will need session graceful migration.

eng-support: account-eng, heads up: enterprise customer "BrightMaps" has 0.9% of sessions pinned to node-g10 and is reporting API timeouts in frontend.

account-eng: pinged customer support and sent proactive message. they're seeing intermittent stalls and one forced reconnect. asking for ETA.

marco: running command to shift non-pinned traffic off GPU cluster to cpu-fallback pool: 
```
redwoodctl split-traffic --from gpu-cluster-east --to cpu-fallback-east --percent 40 --exclude-label "tier=enterprise"
```

tay: deploying temporary lower-max-batch for streaming routers to reduce backlog: 
```
routerctl set streaming_max_batch=8 --for cluster=gpu-cluster-east
```

leah: starting cordon/drain: 
```
kubectl cordon node-g10
kubectl drain node-g10 --force --grace-period=45 --ignore-daemonsets
```

marco: note: some pods fail to reschedule due to GPU allocation constraints; we will evict and fall back to cpu-backup for those. this will cause degraded quality for a subset of requests.

eng-support: BrightMaps impact: p99=2.8s for their streaming endpoints, 0.4% request error. They asked to be moved off pinned nodes asap.

ops-bot: hardware diagnostics pulled: fan_driver_fault, PCIe link retrain attempts=6, ECC_UNCORRECTABLE=2 (recent), ECC_CORRECTABLE spikes earlier. Suggesting board-level hardware failure or riser.

marco: can we attempt remote PCIe retrain / reset before full hardware swap? ops, can you trigger nvidia-smi --gpu-reset?

ops-bot: trying soft reset: 
```
ssh ops@node-g10 sudo nvidia-smi --gpu-reset -i 0
```
Result: reset failed: GPU still unreachable. Proceeding to node isolation.

leah: live mitigation results so far: after shifting 40% traffic and draining node-g10, cluster p99 down to 680ms in 5m. BrightMaps p99 down to 1.1s but still above their SLA.

account-eng: customer replied: appreciate the update, will accept degraded perf for next 2h if we keep them informed. they requested ETA for full resolution.

marco: created hardware ticket DC-WEST-2026-881 for on-site tech replacement. ETA 5h.

tay: for post-incident: we need to add two things: 1) alert on PCIe_link_down events per node (threshold 1/min) and auto-quarantine, 2) plan fast path for session migration of enterprise pinned sessions (staged handoff).

eng-support: also recommend a rollback: add temporary route to redirect only BrightMaps traffic to the already warm cpu-fallback to bring their p99 to under 400ms. We have warmed small-variant models there.

leah: implementing targeted reroute for BrightMaps: 
```
redwoodctl route update --from cluster=gpu-cluster-east --to pool=cpu-fallback-east --match "account=brightmaps" --grace 15s
```

ops-bot: after targeted reroute, BrightMaps p99=360ms. marking as customer SLO satisfied. cluster-wide p99=420ms.

incident-bot: [UPDATE] mitigation applied: targeted reroute id=rt-9002, node-g10 quarantined. Monitoring for 1h.

marco: root cause hypothesis: intermittent PCIe link instability -> driver detach -> GPU unavailability -> kernel-level stalls causing long token generation tail. ECC correctable bursts flagged earlier but uncorrectable events seen later.

tay: action items captured: 
- A1: infra: add PCIe AER alerts + auto-quarantine (owner: ops)
- A2: SRE: implement enterprise session staged migration (owner: tay)
- A3: Runtime: add router backpressure metric for streaming stalls (owner: marco)
- A4: Account: send customer post-incident summary (owner: account-eng)

leah: handing oncall to tay for follow-up monitoring window (30m). i'll coordinate PM with ops for the hardware swap.

tay: taking oncall. current status: BrightMaps SLO met, cluster p99 trending to 380ms. node-g10 remains quarantined and scheduled for return-to-service only after hardware replacement and full burn-in.

incident-bot: [CLOSE?] auto-check in 30m. thread will remain open until hardware ticket resolved.

marco: miscellaneous logs captured for postmortem: /var/log/nvidia/nv-hostengine.log, dmesg snippet, nvml dump. uploading to DC-WEST-2026-881.

eng-support: adding timeline notes: first anomaly observed 4923451500, PCIe link flaps starting 4923453000, elevated p99 detected 4923456789, mitigations started 4923457200.

account-eng: customer confirmed they received our proactive message and accepted the temporary route. they asked for a follow-up engineer call after incident. scheduling.

leah: will write postmortem draft with timeline, impact, and action items. assigning follow-ups per above. closing handoff. :white_check_mark:
